title: Gods of the Household and the State
objective: After this level you can describe early Roman religion, from household spirits to state priests and omens.
summary: Romans kept peace with the gods through correct ritual: household spirits at home, Jupiter on the Capitoline, Vesta’s fire and augury.

cards.headline: Romans rarely asked whether the gods existed. They asked what the gods wanted.
cards.body: Get the ritual right, and the gods stayed on your side. Get it wrong, and even a few birds could hold up the city’s business.

cards.headline: Keeping peace with the gods
cards.body: Roman religion was less about what you believed and more about doing the rituals correctly. The goal had a name: the pax deorum, peace with the gods. Think of it as a contract where the fine print really matters. It started at home. Every household honored the Lares and Penates, guardian spirits of the home and its food store, at a small shrine. Even the pantry had protection.

cards.headline: Gods of the state
cards.body: The city had its own gods to keep happy. On the Capitoline Hill stood Rome’s greatest temple, dedicated to Jupiter, king of the gods, together with Juno and Minerva. Meanwhile, the Vestal Virgins tended the sacred fire of Vesta, goddess of the hearth, day and night. That fire was never allowed to go out. Every home had its little shrine. Rome had a fire nobody was allowed to let die.

cards.fact: Birds could put Roman politics on hold.
cards.context: Before major public decisions, Romans consulted augurs, priests who read the will of the gods in the flight of birds. An unfavorable sign could delay public business. Imagine a big vote postponed because the wrong birds flew by.

cards.headline: Roman religion: understood
learned: Correct ritual kept the peace of the gods
Homes honored the Lares and Penates
Jupiter’s great temple stood on the Capitoline
Vestals kept Vesta’s fire; augurs read birds

questions.prompt: Who kept the sacred fire of Vesta burning?
questions.explanation: The Vestal Virgins tended Vesta’s fire, which was never allowed to go out.

questions.prompt: What was the main aim of Roman religious ritual?

options.label: To keep peace with the gods

questions.explanation: Correct ritual maintained the pax deorum, the peace between Rome and its gods.

questions.prompt: From Level 5: augurs read omens in birds. Which related practice did Romans learn from the Etruscans?

options.label: Reading omens in the stars
options.rationale: Not the Etruscan practice Rome adopted.

questions.explanation: Haruspicy, reading the organs of sacrificed animals, came to Rome from the Etruscans.
